c.tagline: Rugged harbour capital gateway to the world's last frontier.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used; agree on the fare with the driver before departing. Most visitors book taxis through their hotel for safety and fair pricing.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; hotels and tour operators usually have direct contacts for private security/medical assistance.

avoid.reason: Very high crime — carjacking and "raskol" gang robbery/violence; don’t walk, use hotel transport, avoid going out after dark; settlements are no-go

hood_desc: The compact colonial-era harbourfront core with government buildings, banks, Parliament Haus and the main port; convenient base for business travelers.

Port Moresby's main upmarket shopping and dining strip along the waterfront, with a public beach, yacht club and several of the city's better hotels; good for visitors wanting some walkable amenities.
A large government and commercial precinct built in the 1970s with Vision City Mall, ministries and mid-range hotels; practical but car-dependent.
A busy commercial and transit hub near the airport with markets and shopping centres, popular with business travelers needing airport proximity.
A quieter, leafy residential and diplomatic area near the airport with several secure hotels favoured by NGO staff, officials and longer-stay visitors.
lodging: The Sanctuary Hotel Resort and Spa

water.note: Reports on treatment quality are mixed; visitors should stick to bottled or boiled water.

transit.pay: Fares on PMVs and city buses are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in small kina amounts (typically K1-K3 per ride); there is no tap card or app-based ticketing system. Exact change is appreciated. Most visitors instead rely on hotel transport or pre-arranged taxis rather than public buses.
transit.hours: PMVs and buses generally run roughly 6am-6pm; little to no service after dark for safety reasons.
transit.note: Public transport is very basic and not recommended for tourists after dark; most visitors use hotel shuttles, arranged drivers, or taxis booked through their accommodation.

ferry: Coastal ferries to other PNG ports (e.g. Alotau, Lae) depart from Motukea/Port Moresby harbour, mainly for freight/regional travel rather than city transit

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Papua New Guinea; a small tip for exceptional service is appreciated but not required.
